lead: Pakistan's Gulf commitments face a live test today as the Makkah pact committee meets in Riyadh just as Yemen's Saudi-backed government launches an offensive to retake Houthi-held territory, while Tehran ties any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the Islamabad-brokered interim deal with Washington. At home, the collapse of government–PTI talks over counterterrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has put emergency or governor's rule back on the table as the PTI march rolls towards Islamabad. On money, the rupee is holding near Rs277 but analysts expect tight monetary policy to persist, and the government has told the IMF it will sell nine power distributors by December 2027.

stories.headline: Iran links Hormuz reopening to Islamabad interim deal conditions
stories.summary: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until seven conditions in its June interim agreement with the US, known as the Islamabad MoU, are met, according to a Reuters report citing Iran's Nournews carried by Arab News. The statement came days after Tehran received Washington's reply to its latest diplomatic proposal, keeping Pakistan's mediation central to the dispute.

stories.headline: KP emergency back on table after talks collapse over counterterrorism
stories.summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said talks with the opposition had collapsed and accused KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of sabotaging them, while the PTI blamed the Centre's insistence on 'unilateral' counterterrorism action in the province. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, after meeting Naqvi, said he was ready to play his constitutional role if an emergency were deemed necessary.

stories.headline: Eight militants reported killed in Dera Ismail Khan operation
stories.summary: Security forces killed eight militants, including three commanders, in an intelligence-based operation in Dera Ismail Khan, security sources said; the interior ministry identified them as TTP members. Weapons and foreign currency were reportedly recovered.

stories.headline: Yemen government launches offensive to retake Houthi-held territory
stories.summary: The leader of Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced a major military operation to seize all areas under Houthi control, with government forces reporting strikes in Sanaa and Saada, even as the Houthis made fresh ground gains around a government-held city. The escalation adds pressure on Pakistan's commitments under its defence pact with Riyadh.

stories.headline: Makkah pact committee meets in Riyadh today
stories.summary: A committee of the Makkah defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye meets in Riyadh on Monday, the Turkish foreign ministry said, with Turkish ministers including Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan attending. Ankara said the talks would cover recent regional developments and progress in giving the alliance an institutional form.

stories.headline: Government tells IMF nine power distributors will be sold by 2027
stories.summary: Pakistan has given the IMF a December 2027 deadline for privatising nine electricity distribution companies, The Express Tribune reported, an ambitious target for a sector long weighed down by losses.

stories.headline: March fears halt northbound freight, stranding cargo in Karachi
stories.summary: Truckers have stopped journeys northwards from Karachi ahead of the PTI march, leaving cargo stuck at the port city, The Express Tribune reported, adding to supply-chain strain before the goods transporters' strike due on 10 October.

stories.headline: Railways to hand 13 express trains to private operators
stories.summary: Pakistan Railways has ordered officials to complete the outsourcing of 13 express passenger trains by December and is pushing to return idle wagons to service.

stories.headline: FAO says most Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organisation said more than 60% of Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet and called for an overhaul of the country's agrifood system.

stories.headline: Analysts expect tight monetary policy as inflation target slips
stories.summary: With September CPI inflation at 10.3% and oil prices uncertain, analysts told Dawn the State Bank is unlikely to hit its 5–7% medium-term inflation target for FY27, pointing to continued tight policy.

stories.headline: Rupee steady near Rs277 despite oil-driven import bill
stories.summary: The rupee has stayed resilient at about Rs277.1 to the dollar despite higher oil prices and a rising import bill, economists and dealers told Arab News, though they warned a prolonged Middle East conflict could wear down its support.

stories.headline: National Savings to close 111 branches to cut costs
stories.summary: The Central Directorate of National Savings plans to shrink its network from 374 to 263 centres as the government trims operating costs, The Express Tribune reported.

stories.headline: PTI march sets off from Lakki Marwat
stories.summary: Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the PTI's march on Islamabad from Lakki Marwat on Sunday, with the convoy reaching Karak district by night.

stories.headline: Freed MT Honour 25 sailors return to Karachi
stories.summary: Four injured Pakistani crew held for over five months on a ship hijacked by Somali pirates arrived home with the remains of three colleagues.

stories.headline: Cyber agency creates units against 'fake news'
stories.summary: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency said it has set up dedicated units to counter what it called 'fake news' and 'anti-state propaganda'.

stories.headline: Kasur border shooting victims buried
stories.summary: Funeral prayers were held for the two civilians killed by Indian border fire near Kasur, who were buried in their ancestral village.
